memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Moses set out with Joshua his aide, and Moses went up on the mountain of God. He said to the elders, 'Wait here for us until we come back to you. Aaron and Hur are with you, and anyone involved in a dispute can go to them.'" - Exodus 24:13-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before Moses goes up the mountain, he makes careful arrangements. He tells the elders to wait, and he leaves Aaron and Hur in charge to handle any disputes. Moses does not simply disappear into his own spiritual experience and leave the people leaderless. He plans thoughtfully for those under his care, ensuring that needs would still be met while he was away.

There is real wisdom here for anyone who leads or carries responsibility. Moses had been learning to share his burden rather than carry everything alone, and here he practises it well. Godly leadership is not about being indispensable; it is about caring for people so wisely that things do not collapse when you step away. Delegating well is an act of love, not a sign of weakness.

Notice also Joshua, quietly present as Moses' aide. He is not yet a famous leader — he is simply faithful in a supporting role, staying close to the man of God, learning by walking alongside. Years later he would lead the entire nation. Faithfulness in the background is never wasted; God often prepares tomorrow's leaders in today's obscurity (Luke 16:10). Whether you are leading or serving quietly, do it well. God sees, and He is preparing you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I care thoughtfully for those who depend on me, even when I step away?
Am I faithful in supporting roles, trusting God to prepare me in the background?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me lead and serve with care, thinking of others rather than myself. Make me faithful in small and hidden roles, trusting You with what comes next. Amen.
